Its source is a large prominence seen lifting from behind the SW limb starting at 2026-09-26T18:28Z (best seen in GOES SUVI 304), with source location seen on disk, close to the SW limb in STEREO A EUV 304/195 imagery. In EUV A 195 imagery we see an ejecta, as well as dimming and bright post-eruptive arcades. The erupting filament is also seen in AIA 171 and faintly in AIA 304, and ejecta and opening of field lines are seen off/close behind the SW limb in GOES SUVI 286. The erupting filament stretches very approximately from ~S25W15 (mostly dimming) to ~S20W80 (ejecta and post-eruptive arcades), as seen from STEREO A perspective, so the filament can be estimated as centered very approximately at ~S20W135 from the SDO perspective.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2, the front is quite faint but still trackable in early frames.

rows.note: This CME is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to a far-sided filament eruption which begins to lift-off around 2026-10-05T19:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

rows.note: This CME is visible to the west/southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery likely due to a data gap from 2026-10-05T14:38Z to 2026-10-06T01:23Z. The source is a small eruption visible from Active Region 14546 (S19W88) as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery starting around 2026-10-05T23:15Z. A subsequent opening of field lines visible over the southwest limb in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery at this time as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the on-disk source location.

rows.note: Full halo CME in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, first seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2 (shock fully to the E, wide). The source is AR 14549, associated with an M1.4 flare (N10E12) peaking at 2026-10-06T06:10Z, observed in SDO AIA 131. Also observed as an EUV wave, field line movement, brightening, filament ejecta, and small post-eruptive arcade in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304. Additionally observed on the NE limb of STEREO A EUVI 195 as field line movement and EUV wave, and EUVI 304 as filament ejecta.

cmeAnalyses.note: Bulk leading edge triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, noting the slightly distorted shape of the bright LE affecting analysis of the width. This analysis is initially preliminary, but may stand as final LE.

Shock triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, noting the asymmetric shape of the shock especially in the LASCO C2/C3 field-of-view. This analysis is initially preliminary, but may stand as final SH.

rows.note: CME observed to the NE in STEREO A COR2, also faintly observed to the N in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is AR 14549, associated with an M1.8 class flare (N08E07) peaking at 2026-10-06T08:05Z, observed in SDO AIA 131. Also observed as field line movement, EUV wave, dimming, and brightening in SDO AIA 171/193 starting around 2026-10-06T07:52Z, with brightening and filament ejecta in SDO AIA 304. Also observed well in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 starting around 2026-10-06T08:05Z as field line movement and filament ejecta on the NE limb, with some northward deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation betweeen SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The CME front is much more faint in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, so the width in COR2 is used primarily.

rows.note: Faint CME first seen to the NNE by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-10-06T13:08Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this CME is faint field line opening seen originating from approx. E10N40 beginning at approx. 2026-10-06T12:22Z as seen in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
